page: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the 64-bit ARM (arm64) processor architecture, coupled with 384.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core, addressing large-footprint applications requiring generous RAM-to-CPU proportions.

For fast local I/O requirements, the instance includes 2832 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units, prioritizing general system memory and processor throughput instead. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage options for external persistent disk attachments alongside its bundled high-speed local disk capacity.

The 64-bit ARM architecture delivers competitive resource efficiency, maximizing memory density per core while maintaining high compute availability across all 48 dedicated threads. Workloads requiring x86 instruction sets or vector instruction extensions such as AVX are not supported, making ARM-native compilation necessary. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, distributed data analysis frameworks, and transactional database servers relying on fast local storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs on the arm64 architecture and 384.0 GB of system memory. Delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is designed for demanding memory-bound enterprise applications. Hardware resources include a bundled 2832 GB NVMe SSD local disk that provides fast temporary storage and low-latency disk I/O, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not feature discrete GPU accelerators. By pairing power-efficient ARM compute cores with substantial physical memory and high-capacity NVMe storage, the configuration achieves a dense, cost-effective resource profile for memory-heavy computing. It is well suited for deploying in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, big data analytics engines, and transactional database management systems.
